goal: Step an MCP tasks-extension task to its next state, so a client polling tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel always sees the state the protocol core would write.

app.name: mcp-task-lifecycle
app.title: MCP task lifecycle
app.purpose: Give the next state of an io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks task from its current state, the step applied to it (settle, answer or cancel), what its plan still asks, the clock and how many input keys remain unanswered.
limits: It does not create a task: a task starts working, as the seed of its tool's plan, when tools/call decides to answer a task.
It does not expire a task: a task past its ttlMs is dropped from the host's table by the next request, outside this step.
It does not check the host's clock or table; the host owes the core exactly the table it was given.

fields.name: state
fields.means: the task's current status, as DetailedTask in src/Tasks.lex.tex

fields.name: event
fields.means: the step: settle (tasks/get), answer (tasks/update with every given key) or cancel (tasks/cancel)

fields.name: asks
fields.means: whether the task's plan still holds input requests to park on (parkedPlan empties them once it parks)

fields.name: elapsed
fields.means: milliseconds since the task was created, now_ms less createdMs

fields.name: deadline
fields.means: milliseconds after creation the plan's next step is due: parkAfterMs when it asks, finishAfterMs otherwise

fields.name: outcome
fields.means: how the plan concludes: PlanOutcome.completes with a result or PlanOutcome.fails with a JSON-RPC error

fields.name: remaining
fields.means: input keys still unanswered after this answer

meanings.working: the task is running; tasks/get answers status working
meanings.input-required: the task waits for the client to answer its inputRequests through tasks/update
meanings.completed: terminal: the plan's result is the task's result
meanings.failed: terminal: the task carries the plan's JSON-RPC error
meanings.cancelled: terminal: the client cancelled the task before it finished

rules.why: src/Tasks.lex.tex: settle, answer and cancel keep a completed entry (kept entry)
src/Tasks.lex.tex: a failed task is terminal (isTerminal), and every step keeps it
src/Tasks.lex.tex: a cancelled task is terminal, and every step keeps it
Tasks.cancel settles first: work that finished before the cancel stays completed (TASKS.md, What a task does)
Tasks.cancel settles first: work that failed before the cancel stays failed
Tasks.cancelSettled: a working or input_required task becomes cancelled
Tasks.settleWorking: a plan that parks moves to input_required once parkAfterMs has passed
Tasks.settleWorking: with nothing to ask, the task concludes once finishAfterMs has passed (Tasks.due)
Tasks.concluded: a plan that fails gives a failed task with its JSON-RPC error
Tasks.resume settles at once: a plan that still asks parks again
Tasks.answerInput: the last key answered resumes the task, which settles at once and completes if due
Tasks.answerInput: the last key answered resumes the task, which settles at once and fails if due
Tasks.resume: with every key answered and nothing due, the task returns to working
Tasks.settle keeps an input_required task, and answerInput keeps it while any key remains

app.otherwiseWhy: src/Tasks.lex.tex: a working task whose next step is not yet due, or that is answered, is kept as it is

properties.why: TASKS.md: a cancel never leaves a task running
a cancel never leaves a task waiting for input
Tasks.due: no work concludes before finishAfterMs has passed
Tasks.due: no work fails before finishAfterMs has passed
Tasks.answerInput: a task resumes only once every key is answered
Tasks.settle: settling a task that waits for input changes nothing

stakeholders.name: MCP client author
stakeholders.text: Polls a task through tasks/get, answers it through tasks/update and cancels it through tasks/cancel, and needs every answer to be the state the protocol allows.

stakeholders.name: Host adapter author
stakeholders.text: Holds the task table between requests for the stateless core (PrismPM issue 216) and needs a finished task to stay finished whatever arrives next.

concerns.name: Terminal tasks stay terminal
concerns.text: A completed, failed or cancelled task is never moved again by settle, answer or cancel.

components.name: MCP client
components.text: The client that declares io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in its request _meta and calls tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel.

components.name: Host adapter
components.text: PrismPM's adapter (issue 216): it sends now_ms, the fresh task id and the task table in every request frame and stores the table the core returns.

components.name: MCP conformance suite
components.text: modelcontextprotocol/conformance at cf022cbb, whose tasks scenarios drive the conformance build.

threats.name: Terminal task revived
threats.text: A step moves a completed, failed or cancelled task back to working, so a client sees finished work run again.

control.name: Final states proved
control.text: The machine declares completed, failed and cancelled final; the builder checks every sampled step keeps them and Lean proves it for every request.

threats.name: Cancel hides finished work
threats.text: A cancel that arrives after the work finished reports cancelled, and the client loses a result it was owed.

control.name: Settle before cancel
control.text: tasks/cancel settles first, so work already due concludes and the cancel leaves it.

threats.name: Host clock or table substituted
threats.text: The host sends a clock that runs backward or a table other than the one it was given, so a task concludes early or reappears.
threats.accepted: The core keeps no state by design; TASKS.md puts the clock and the table in the host's custody, and the host owes the core exactly what it was given.

quality.text: Each acceptance vector answers the state Tasks.settle, Tasks.answer or Tasks.cancel writes.
quality.measureText: Acceptance vectors whose replayed answer differs from the expected next state.

quality.text: No step takes a completed, failed or cancelled task to another state.
quality.measureText: Sampled steps from a final state whose answer is another state.
